analysis.title: Market Know-How 4Q 2026: Yield Ahead
key_insights: GSAM argues the era of central bank yield suppression is over and the bond market has resumed setting yields, which it calls a regime change rather than a cyclical blip.
G10 yields face pressure from resilient growth, energy market volatility and heavy AI-related borrowing.

Base case is a reflationary backdrop led by resilient growth and AI momentum despite higher rates. GSAM stays constructive on risk assets in the medium term but sees fewer short-term opportunities and higher risks.

Developed market growth is supported by expansionary fiscal policy, the AI investment cycle and stable labor markets. GSAM's monthly activity indicator has G4 growth tracking at 2%, above trend, and it expects that to persist into year-end.
Germany's deficit is set to widen from 3% of GDP last year to nearly 4% in 2026. The US 'One Big Beautiful Bill' extended income tax cuts and added targeted credits.
GSAM expects a shallow developed-market hiking cycle followed by a prolonged pause. It calls the inflation drivers 'HEAT': Harvests, Energy, AI and Trade.
GSAM projects inflation staying above 3% across most developed markets near term, with a return to target delayed until at least 2028.
GSAM expects 1 to 2 more rate hikes from major central banks by year-end. Projected policy rates are ECB 2.75-3.00%, Fed 4.25-4.50% (upper bound), BoE 4.00-4.25% and BoJ 1.50-1.75%.

US hyperscalers have raised about $400B in the US IG corporate bond market this year, roughly 20% of gross issuance. AI-related bonds run 3 to 4 years longer in maturity than the IG index, which pushes up long-end yields.
US AI hyperscaler capex is estimated at 1.8% of GDP and could rise to 2.5%-3.5%.

Elections are an additional source of bond yield pressure. More than 40% of the world's population and about 50% of global GDP vote in national elections through the end of 2027. The US midterms are on November 3, and polls point to gridlock with Democrats retaking the House.

Historically, election-year fiscal slippage averages only 0.25% of GDP in structural primary balance. GSAM sees fragmented parliaments and gridlock, not spending giveaways, as the main 2027 fiscal risk.

Long-term, GSAM expects a persistently positive and rising term premium to drive yields and volatility. Causes cited are high debt, defense and AI spending needs, declining official-sector demand, geopolitical supply shocks, less Fed forward guidance and price-sensitive private buyers absorbing issuance.
Portfolio implications: manage duration more actively, diversify curve positioning, and hold more inflation protection within fixed income.

Inflation Re-acceleration scenario: larger energy spillovers force aggressive tightening and growth weakens. GSAM would favor short-duration fixed income, high-dividend equities and credit over equities, expects Europe to outperform, and sees bear-flattening curves.
Rapid Disinflation scenario: faster energy supply growth lets central banks pivot sooner. Dollar weakness favors ex-US equities and small caps, core fixed income benefits, and curves bull-steepen.

GSAM keeps high conviction in EM equities on AI capex, but rotates from mega-cap hyperscalers toward US small caps. It likes EM debt for carry, and hedge funds plus private credit to mitigate drawdowns when equity and bond volatility rise together.
EM debt carry: the breakeven analysis measures how much of a Treasury sell-off the starting yield can absorb before duration turns total return negative.
Economic security equities are framed as a play on the capex cycle that geopolitical risk is driving, in energy, resources and critical infrastructure.
Liquid alternatives are pitched as diversification for months when equities and Treasuries sell off together. In those months the S&P 500 averaged -3.7% and the 10Y UST -1.8%.

tension_points.bull_case: Energy flows normalize, growth stays resilient, inflation returns to target slowly and central banks only tighten modestly, supporting risk assets through AI-driven earnings.
tension_points.bear_case: Energy-crisis spillovers are larger than expected, inflation stays higher for longer, central banks tighten aggressively and traditional hedges lose their edge.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Energy flows failing to normalize toward pre-war levels in the coming months.
